proof:
Conventions (used throughout). n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ 0 are integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (equal to Simon's Hⁿ), B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ (closed ball), ω_n = omega n ∈ (0, ∞), and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for every n-dimensional subspace P. For a rectifiable n-varifold V: μ = μ_V = V.weight; T_x = V.tangentSpace x; p_x and p_x^⊥ are the orthogonal projections onto T_x and T_x^⊥; div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x = trace(DX(x)∘p_x); ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x = p_x(∇h(x)); r = |x − ξ|; q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² ∈ [0, 1] (q_ξ(ξ) = 0 because division by 0 is 0); w_ξ(x) = q_ξ(x)/|x − ξ|ⁿ (w_ξ(ξ) = 0); a_ξ(ρ) = μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ (a real number); Θ(ξ) = V.density ξ. A test field in U is a C¹ map X: E → E with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField). 'V has mean curvature H in U' (HasMeanCurvatureIn) means H ∈ L¹_loc(U, μ) and ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every test field X in U; 'stationary in U' means ∫div_M X dμ = 0 for every test field X in U. (FV) for V means: (FV1) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K; (FV2) dim T_x = n for μ-a.e. x; (FV3) x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. (GF) is the statement that (FV) holds for every n ≥ 1, every ℓ and every V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ (exactly the second conjunct of the sibling tangent_structure_first_variation); (AT) is the contract Prop ApproxTangentAE. Under (FV): q_ξ, w_ξ, ∇^M h (for h ∈ C¹(U), on U) and div_M X (for X ∈ C¹) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous functions of p_x and of continuous data; |div_M X| ≤ (n+ℓ)‖DX‖ and div_M X = 0 off tsupport X, so div_M X is μ-integrable for every test field X; μ is a locally finite, hence outer regular, Borel measure, and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (spt V = spt μ).

Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.14–3.18 and 4.1–4.9, with the documented errata: with the sign convention 3.14(‡) the error term of 3.16/4.1 enters with a plus sign and the integrating factor is exp(−∫E); κ = (p − n)/(4p) in 4.2 (the printed p/(4(p − n)) does not give ∫_0^ρ|F_0| ≤ ½Λ(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}); the remark after 3.17 concerns U (not N ∩ U). The printed proofs apply an ε-dependent integrating factor before letting ε ↓ 0, which leaves F dependent on the cutoff. To obtain one F we take the limit ε ↓ 0 first — this is the sibling weighted_monotonicity_identity, i.e. 3.16/4.1 integrated from σ to ρ with ε ↓ 0 — and then apply the integrating factor to the integrated identity by the integration-by-parts Lemma of Step 2 (the product rule for the BV function ρ ↦ ρ^{-n}μ(B_ρ) and the absolutely continuous factor F). The bounds on F, E and G are the printed ones.

Assume (GF). Fix n ≥ 1, ℓ, V, an open U, H such that V has mean curvature H in U, and write μ = μ_V.

Step 1 (basic identity). Let B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, ρ > 0, a := a_ξ, D(s, t) := ∫_{B_t∖B_s} w_ξ dμ ≥ 0 and e(τ) := τ^{-n-1}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ dμ. For 0 < s ≤ t ≤ ρ:
(1.1) a(t) − a(s) = D(s, t) + ∫_{(s,t]} e(τ) dτ.
This is weighted_monotonicity_identity with h ≡ 1 (C¹; tsupport h ∩ B_t(ξ) ⊆ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U), because ∫_{B_τ}1 dμ = μ(B_τ), ∇^M 1 = 0 and 1·H = H; its hypotheses (FV1)–(FV3) come from (GF). It also gives integrability of e on (s, t] and of w_ξ on B_t ∖ B_s. On [s, t], a and e are bounded Borel functions: τ ↦ μ(B_τ) is nondecreasing, τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ}⟨x − ξ, H⟩ dμ is the difference of the nondecreasing functions τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ} g⁺ dμ and τ ↦ ∫_{B_τ} g⁻ dμ with g := ⟨x − ξ, H⟩ ∈ L¹(μ⌞B_ρ), and |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-n}∫_{B_ρ}|H| dμ.

Step 2 (integration by parts). Let 0 < σ ≤ ρ with (1.1) on [σ, ρ], and let F: [σ, ρ] → ℝ be absolutely continuous, F(t) = F(σ) + ∫_σ^t F'(τ) dτ with F' ∈ L¹(σ, ρ). Then
(2.1) F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|) w_ξ(x) dμ(x) + ∫_σ^ρ (F(τ)e(τ) + F'(τ)a(τ)) dτ.
Proof: F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) + (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ), and by (1.1) (F(ρ) − F(σ))a(ρ) = ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)[a(t) + D(t, ρ) + ∫_t^ρ e(s) ds] dt. As x ∈ B_ρ ∖ B_t iff t < |x − ξ| ≤ ρ, Fubini for the integrable function (t, x) ↦ F'(t)w_ξ(x)1_{t<|x−ξ|} on (σ, ρ] × (B_ρ ∖ B_σ) gives ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)D(t, ρ) dt = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} w_ξ(x)(F(|x − ξ|) − F(σ)) dμ(x), and Fubini on {σ < t < s ≤ ρ} gives ∫_σ^ρ F'(t)∫_t^ρ e(s) ds dt = ∫_σ^ρ e(s)(F(s) − F(σ)) ds. Adding these to F(σ)(a(ρ) − a(σ)) = F(σ)D(σ, ρ) + F(σ)∫_σ^ρ e, the terms containing F(σ) cancel, which gives (2.1).

Step 3 (BoundedCurvatureMonotonicity, 3.16–3.17). Assume Λ ≥ 0 and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e. in U. Fix ξ, R with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U. If R ≤ 0, take F ≡ 1 and G ≡ 1 (all conditions are vacuous). Let R > 0; for τ ∈ (0, R), a and e are as in Step 1 (B_τ(ξ) ⊆ U). For μ-a.e. x ∈ B_τ(ξ), |⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ τΛ, hence |e(τ)| ≤ Λa(τ). Put E(τ) := e(τ)/a(τ) if a(τ) ≠ 0 and E(τ) := 0 otherwise: E is Borel on (0, R), |E| ≤ Λ, and e = Ea everywhere (if a(τ) = 0 then μ(B_τ) = 0 and e(τ) = 0). Define F(ρ) := exp(−∫_{(0,ρ]} E(τ) dτ) for 0 < ρ < R and F(ρ) := 1 otherwise; then F(ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λρ}, e^{Λρ}] for ρ ∈ (0, R). On [σ, ρ] ⊂ (0, R), Φ(t) := ∫_{(0,t]} E is Λ-Lipschitz with Φ' = E a.e. (Lebesgue differentiation), so F = exp(−Φ) is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous, with F' = −EF a.e. For 0 < σ ≤ ρ < R, (2.1) applies and Fe + F'a = F(e − Ea) = 0 a.e., so F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|)w_ξ dμ. On B_ρ ∖ B_σ, |x − ξ| ∈ (σ, ρ] ⊂ (0, R), so e^{−ΛR}D(σ, ρ) ≤ ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|)w_ξ dμ ≤ e^{ΛR}D(σ, ρ). Define G(σ, ρ) := D(σ, ρ)^{-1}∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|)w_ξ dμ if D(σ, ρ) ≠ 0 and G(σ, ρ) := 1 otherwise. Then G(σ, ρ) ∈ [e^{−ΛR}, e^{ΛR}] and F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = G(σ, ρ)D(σ, ρ) (if D(σ, ρ) = 0 both sides vanish). This is the first conjunct.
Density and upper semicontinuity (remark after 3.17, on U). For ξ ∈ U choose R > 0 with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U. By the identity, ρ ↦ F(ρ)a(ρ) is nondecreasing and ≥ 0 on (0, R), so it has a limit L ≥ 0 as ρ ↓ 0; since F(ρ) → 1, a(ρ) → L, i.e. V.HasDensityAt ξ (L/ω_n) and Θ(ξ) = L/ω_n. Moreover ω_nΘ(ξ) ≤ F(ρ)a(ρ) ≤ e^{Λρ}a_ξ(ρ) for 0 < ρ < R. Upper semicontinuity: let ξ ∈ U, t > Θ(ξ); choose R > 0 with B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U, then ρ ∈ (0, R/2) with e^{Λρ}μ(B_ρ(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t, then δ ∈ (0, R/2) with e^{Λρ}μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t (continuity from above, μ(B_{2R}(ξ)) < ∞). For |η − ξ| < δ: B_R(η) ⊆ U, ρ < R and B_ρ(η) ⊆ B_{ρ+δ}(ξ), so Θ(η) ≤ e^{Λρ}μ(B_ρ(η))/(ω_nρⁿ) < t.

Step 4 (LogarithmicMonotonicityError, 3.18). Let B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, 0 < σ < ρ, and τ^{1−n}∫_{B_τ(ξ)}|H| dμ ≤ δ for τ ∈ [σ, ρ]. By (1.1), a(ρ) − a(σ) − D(σ, ρ) = ∫_{(σ,ρ]} e. For τ ∈ (σ, ρ], |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-n-1}·τ∫_{B_τ}|H| dμ = τ^{-1}·τ^{1−n}∫_{B_τ}|H| dμ ≤ δ/τ. Hence |a(ρ) − a(σ) − D(σ, ρ)| ≤ ∫_σ^ρ δτ^{-1} dτ = δ log(ρ/σ).

Step 5 (LpMonotonicity, 4.2–4.8). Let p > n, H ∈ L^p_loc(U) (IsLocallyLp), R > 0, B_R(ξ) ⊆ U and A := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(ξ)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ κΛ with κ = lpKappa n p = (p − n)/(4p) > 0. Since A ≥ 0, Λ ≥ 0. Note p > n ≥ 1, ∫_{B_R}|H|^p dμ < ∞ (B_R(ξ) is a compact subset of U), and (∫_{B_R}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} = A R^{n/p−1}.
(5.1) (4.2–4.3 at ε = 0, Hölder.) For τ ∈ (0, R]: |e(τ)| ≤ τ^{-n}∫_{B_τ}|H| dμ ≤ τ^{-n}(∫_{B_R}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} μ(B_τ)^{1−1/p} = A R^{n/p−1} τ^{−n/p} a(τ)^{1−1/p} ≤ (κΛ/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + a(τ)), using μ(B_τ) = τⁿa(τ) and b^{1−1/p} ≤ 1 + b for b ≥ 0.
(5.2) (4.5.) Put F_0(τ) := e(τ)/(1 + a(τ)) for τ ∈ (0, R]. Then |F_0(τ)| ≤ (κΛ/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}, which is integrable on (0, R] since n/p < 1, and ∫_{(0,ρ]}|F_0| ≤ κΛ (p/(p − n))(ρ/R)^{1−n/p} = (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p} ≤ (Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p} (corrected κ). Define F(ρ) := exp(−∫_{(0,ρ]} F_0) for 0 < ρ ≤ R and F(ρ) := 1 otherwise. For ρ ∈ (0, R]: e^{−(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}} ≤ F(ρ) ≤ e^{(Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}}, and with s := −∫_{(0,ρ]} F_0, |s| ≤ (Λ/4)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p} ≤ Λ/4, so |F(ρ) − 1| = |e^s − 1| ≤ e^{|s|}|s| ≤ e^{Λ/4}(Λ/4)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p} ≤ (e^{Λ/2}/2)Λ(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}.
(5.3) (4.4, 4.7.) On [σ, ρ] ⊆ (0, R], Φ_0(t) := ∫_{(0,t]} F_0 is absolutely continuous with Φ_0' = F_0 a.e., so F = exp(−Φ_0) is absolutely continuous with F' = −F_0F a.e. Since e = F_0(1 + a), Fe + F'a = F(e − F_0a) = FF_0 = −F' a.e. By (1.1) (valid because B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U) and (2.1), F(ρ)a(ρ) − F(σ)a(σ) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|)w_ξ dμ − (F(ρ) − F(σ)), i.e., with E := F − 1,
(F(ρ)a(ρ) + E(ρ)) − (F(σ)a(σ) + E(σ)) = ∫_{B_ρ∖B_σ} F(|x − ξ|)w_ξ dμ for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ R.
On B_ρ ∖ B_σ, |x − ξ| ∈ (0, R], so F(|x − ξ|) ∈ [e^{−Λ/2}, e^{Λ/2}] ⊆ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}]; defining G(σ, ρ) as in Step 3 (the ratio, or 1 when D(σ, ρ) = 0) gives G(σ, ρ) ∈ [e^{−Λ}, e^{Λ}] and identity 4.7. (4.8) Since G·D ≥ 0, ρ ↦ F(ρ)a(ρ) + F(ρ) − 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R].

Step 6 (LpDensity, 4.9). Let p > n and H ∈ L^p_loc(U). Existence: for ξ ∈ U choose R > 0 with B_R(ξ) ⊆ U, let A be as in Step 5 and Λ := A/κ. By Step 5, Ψ(ρ) := F(ρ)a(ρ) + F(ρ) − 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R] and Ψ ≥ F − 1 ≥ e^{−Λ/2} − 1 > −1, so Ψ(ρ) → L as ρ ↓ 0; since F(ρ) → 1, a(ρ) = (Ψ(ρ) + 1 − F(ρ))/F(ρ) → L. Hence V.HasDensityAt ξ (L/ω_n) and Θ(ξ) = L/ω_n. Upper semicontinuity: let ξ ∈ U and t > Θ(ξ). Choose R > 0 with B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U, put A_0 := (R^{p−n}∫_{B_{2R}(ξ)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} and Λ := A_0/κ. For every η ∈ B_R(ξ), B_R(η) ⊆ B_{2R}(ξ) ⊆ U and (R^{p−n}∫_{B_R(η)}|H|^p dμ)^{1/p} ≤ A_0 = κΛ, so Step 5 applies at the centre η with radius R and this Λ, giving F_η with the bounds of (5.2); by (4.8) at η, for ρ ∈ (0, R]: ω_nΘ(η) = lim_{s↓0}Ψ_η(s) ≤ Ψ_η(ρ) ≤ e^{c(ρ)}a_η(ρ) + (e^{c(ρ)} − 1), where c(ρ) := (Λ/2)(ρ/R)^{1−n/p}. Choose ρ ∈ (0, R/2] with e^{c(ρ)}μ(B_ρ(ξ))/ρⁿ + e^{c(ρ)} − 1 < ω_n t (the left side tends to ω_nΘ(ξ) as ρ ↓ 0), then δ ∈ (0, R/2) with e^{c(ρ)}μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/ρⁿ + e^{c(ρ)} − 1 < ω_n t (continuity from above). For |η − ξ| < δ, a_η(ρ) ≤ μ(B_{ρ+δ}(ξ))/ρⁿ, hence Θ(η) < t. So Θ is upper semicontinuous on U. Steps 3–6 prove the four conjuncts.
key_steps: weighted_monotonicity_identity with h ≡ 1: a(t) − a(s) = D(s,t) + ∫_{(s,t]} e for balls inside U
Integration by parts against an absolutely continuous factor F (Fubini on annuli and triangles)
3.17: E = e/a with |E| ≤ Λ, F = exp(−∫E), Fe + F'a = 0, so F a increases with ratio G ∈ [e^{−ΛR}, e^{ΛR}]; density and u.s.c. from the monotone F a
3.18: |e(τ)| ≤ δ/τ on [σ, ρ] integrates to δ log(ρ/σ)
4.2–4.8: Hölder gives |e| ≤ (κΛ/R)(τ/R)^{−n/p}(1 + a); F_0 = e/(1+a), F = exp(−∫F_0) with corrected κ bounds; Fe + F'a = −F' gives 4.7 and 4.8 up to ρ = R
4.9: monotone Ψ = F a + F − 1 with uniform Λ near ξ gives existence and upper semicontinuity of Θ
